prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single universally “best” company — the best choice depends on your exact location, roof type (shingles, tile, metal, flat), budget, insurance situation, and timeline. I can help you find top local options if you tell me your ZIP code and roof type. Meanwhile, here’s how to pick the best Miami roofer for a hurricane-rated replacement and a ready-to-use vetting checklist.

What to require from any candidate roofer
- Florida licensed & insured roofing contractor (verify license on Florida DBPR).  
- Worker’s compensation and general liability insurance (ask for certificates).  
- Experience with Miami-Dade County product approvals (NOA) and Florida Building Code high-wind installations.  
- Use of hurricane-rated materials (Miami-Dade NOA-rated shingles/tiles/metal and high-wind underlayments, approved fasteners/clips/straps).  
- Written permit handling and inspection process included.  
- Clear, itemized written estimate with scope, materials (brand/model), wind rating, fastening pattern, flashing details, and timeline.  
- Manufacturer’s warranty (30-year/lifetime where available) + contractor workmanship warranty (5–10+ years).  
- Clear payment schedule, lien releases, and change-order procedures.  
- References for recent hurricane-rated full replacements in Miami — ask for addresses so you can inspect.

Top questions to ask each contractor
1. Are you licensed in Florida as a roofing contractor? (Get license number and verify.)  
2. Can you provide current certificates for liability insurance and worker’s comp?  
3. Do you install products with Miami-Dade NOA approvals? Which products will you use? (Ask for NOA numbers.)  
4. What wind rating will this roof assembly meet? (e.g., 120 mph+, specify uplift resistance and test standard)  
5. Will the installation follow manufacturer installation instructions and FBC/NOA details?  
6. Who pulls permits and handles inspections? (They should do it.)  
7. What is included in the scope (decking replacement, underlayment, ice/water/secondary barrier, flashing, vents, ridge, ridge vents, drip edge, gutters if applicable)?  
8. What warranties do you provide (workmanship length and transferability)?  
9. Can you provide at least 3 recent customer references and photos of completed Miami hurricane-rated jobs?  
10. What is your payment schedule? (Avoid large up-front payments; final payment after certificate of completion/inspection is preferred.)

Red flags
- Unwilling/unable to provide license/insurance info for verification.  
- Demanding large cash up front or only cash payments.  
- Very low bid with vague scope — likely cutting corners.  
- No Miami-Dade NOA knowledge or refusal to use NOA-listed products when required.  
- No written contract or unwillingness to sign.

Where to find highly rated local contractors
- Verify license: Florida DBPR (online).  
- Check project history and reviews on Google, BBB, Yelp, Houzz, Remodeling/Angi.  
- Ask local building supply houses for referrals (they sell to reputable roofers).  
- Check Miami-Dade County permit records to confirm similar jobs and inspections.

If you want, I can:
- Find and shortlist 3–5 top-rated Miami roofing contractors (I’ll need your ZIP code and roof type), or  
- Draft an email/phone script and a side‑by‑side estimate comparison template you can use when contacting contractors.

Which would you like me to do next? If you want company names, please tell me your ZIP code and the roof material (shingle, tile, metal, flat/membrane) and whether this will be handled through insurance.
